fields.features_heading: Six Parts of Conference Week in One App
fields.features_subheading: A paper sign-up sheet on the classroom door handles one job. Emergent builds the app that books each meeting and follows up.
fields.feature_1:
Slots that close as families book

Set the evenings, the slot length, and a 5-minute gap between meetings. Once a family books 4:20, that time drops off the list for every other parent who opens the form.
fields.feature_2:
Siblings booked back to back

Parents with two children at the school book both teachers in one pass. The form offers only adjacent times, and the family walks from one classroom to the next without a long wait.
fields.feature_3:
Questions answered at home first

Write the questions you want answered before the meeting. Parents reply when they book, and you read each answer beside that family's slot before their 15 minutes start.
fields.feature_4:
Email reminders the day before

The app emails each family their time and room the day before the conference. A parent who cancels from that email frees the slot, and the next family to open the form can take it.
fields.feature_5:
Notes saved under each student

Every conference note is saved under the student's name in a database you own. Before spring conferences, open the fall notes to see the goal you set and if the check-in happened.
fields.feature_6:
Code your district can host

On paid plans, export the full codebase to your GitHub repository. A district IT team can then run the conference app on its own servers and keep building on it from there.

fields.tab_content_1:
Three families still have no slot on conference night

Faustina Szabo-Reyes has 24 families at Briarmoss Elementary. She opens 28 slots of 15 minutes across 2 evenings. Once a family books, that slot disappears for everyone else. So far 21 of the 24 families have booked, and 7 slots are still open. The app emails the 3 families without a slot a reminder listing the open times.
fields.tab_content_2:
Damaris reads every answer the night before

Damaris Peake teaches kindergarten at Pinehaven Elementary. Her booking confirmation asks parents 4 short questions. By the night before conferences, 19 of her 22 families have answered. The Lowenthal family wrote that their son pushes back on bedtime reading, and that note sits beside their 4:30 PM slot.
fields.tab_content_3:
Seven interpreter requests, sorted by language on one list

Plover Creek Elementary adds a question to its conference sign-up asking which families need an interpreter, and in which language. Of the 31 families booked, 7 asked for one: 4 in Spanish, 2 in Vietnamese, and 1 in Arabic. Each request emails the office manager with the teacher, the room, and the slot time.
fields.tab_content_4:
Which goal did the family pick? The email says

Thorold Vantwest teaches math at Inglenook Middle School and types while the parents talk. The notes form asks for a strength, a goal, and the plan at home. For Thisbe Garside, the goal is to hand in all 5 homework sets each week. At 6:00 PM the app emails her parents the summary, with a check-in date 6 weeks out.

fields.howto_title: How to Build Parent Conference Forms
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to build parent conference forms for teachers that offer each family a time, hear their concerns first, and follow up.
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Describe the week in a prompt
fields.howto_step_1_des: Count the families you need to see, then add 4 or 5 spare slots for reschedules. Pick one slot length for everyone, and leave a 5-minute gap between meetings for notes. Spread the slots over 2 evenings if working parents need later times.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Keep it to 4 short questions or fewer, sent with the booking confirmation. Lead with the topic the parent cares about most. Give each question an open text box, since a checkbox rarely tells you what is worrying a family.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Add a question about the language spoken at home and whether anyone coming needs an interpreter. Route each yes to whoever arranges interpreters, along with where and when the meeting happens, well before the first evening.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Tell Emergent how many evenings you have, how long each meeting runs, what parents should answer, and who gets each email. It builds the sign-up form, your teacher view, and a database for the responses. To change any part later, describe the change in a new prompt.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Decide what the notes email carries
fields.howto_step_5_des: Choose what parents receive after each conference. A strength, a goal, the plan at home, and a check-in date fit on one screen of a phone. Send it the same evening, while the conversation is still fresh for everyone.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Book a slot yourself as a parent would
fields.howto_step_6_des: Open the link on a phone and book a time as a parent. Check that the slot disappears for the next person and that the confirmation email arrives with the questions. Then cancel and confirm that the slot opens again.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Share the link and watch it fill
fields.howto_step_7_des: Post the link where families already look, such as the class newsletter. Check the schedule a few days later, then send the reminder to families who have not booked while there are still open slots to choose from.

faq_plan.q: What is parent conference forms for teachers?
faq_plan.a: Parent conference forms for teachers are the forms a teacher runs around a parent-teacher meeting. A sign-up lets families pick a time, a short questionnaire gathers their concerns beforehand, and a notes record captures what both sides agreed. Some schools add an interpreter request.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up parent conference forms for teachers?
faq_plan.a: Describe your conference week to Emergent's AI form builder: the evenings, the slot length, the questions for parents, and who gets each email. It builds the sign-up, your schedule, and the database behind them. Book a test slot on your phone before the link goes home.

faq_plan.q: How long should each time slot be on parent conference forms for teachers?
faq_plan.a: Plan 15 minutes for a routine conference and 20 to 30 for a family with a bigger concern. A 5-minute gap keeps one long meeting from pushing every later family back. Emergent can build the sign-up so a family books 2 slots in a row when they need more time.

faq_plan.q: How do parents pick a meeting time on parent conference forms for teachers?
faq_plan.a: They open a link, see the open times, and pick one. Send a confirmation with the room number and a link to change the booking. It works much like a conference registration form for a professional event, with short meetings in place of sessions.

faq_plan.q: What questions for parents belong on parent conference forms for teachers?
faq_plan.a: Start with the one thing the parent most wants to discuss. Then ask about homework routines and any recent change at home, such as a move or a new sibling. Read the answers the night before and open the meeting on the parent's question.

faq_plan.q: Can parent conference forms for teachers handle interpreter requests?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Ask about language on the sign-up itself, then send each request to the person who books interpreters. Group requests by language so one interpreter can cover back-to-back meetings. Emergent keeps the request list in a database you own, with a count for each language.

faq_plan.q: Should parent conference forms for teachers also collect permission slips?
faq_plan.a: No, keep the two apart. A conference sign-up gathers a time and a few questions, while a field trip or a class photo needs its own signed record. Send a parent consent form for that, and keep the sign-up about the meeting.

faq_plan.q: What notes should go on parent conference forms for teachers after the meeting?
faq_plan.a: Write the goal in words the family used and agreed to, not in report-card terms. Keep it short enough to read on a phone. Add the date you will check in, and note anything the family asked you to follow up on.

faq_plan.q: Can parent conference forms for teachers handle every class in a school?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Give each teacher a list of slots and a room, and let families with more than one child book teachers back to back. Emergent builds the school-wide version from the same prompt, with no response caps as more classes join.

faq_plan.q: Can parent conference forms for teachers track take-home reading kits?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Add a question asking whether the family wants a kit, hand it over at the meeting, and keep a list of who has one. For anything valuable, such as a tablet, use an equipment rental agreement form that records the item and its return date.

plan.angle: Searchers for parent conference forms for teachers mostly find printable templates and generic form-tool galleries: a single sheet for notes or a blank sign-up grid. A teacher running conference week actually needs four connected pieces: a slot sign-up that hides taken times, a short questionnaire parents answer before they arrive, an interpreter request that reaches the front office, and a notes record that goes home the same evening with a check-in date. This page shows all four working off one schedule and one database, with email reminders, so the page wins on the workflow the templates leave out.
